inspection_summary: Inspected all 497 normalized lines. The paper compares zero ordinates of two primitive Dirichlet L-functions through coincidence, intervening-zero, and index-displacement questions, then connects moment estimates for argument-function differences to positive-proportion separation and an almost-all displacement bound. OCR is prose-readable but formula-poor: only mechanisms recoverable from the checked text are selected, and every formula-sensitive candidate requires scan verification before training use.

accepted_units.title: Three relative-zero questions for two Dirichlet L-functions
accepted_units.why_material: Separates coincidence of zeros, existence of an intervening zero, and the indexed displacement A_n as distinct comparison problems rather than treating zero separation as one undifferentiated property.
accepted_units.context_note: The symbols for characters and zero ordinates are OCR-corrupted, but the prose definitions and the role of A_n are recoverable from these lines.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on ordered zero ordinates and multiplicity; verify displayed inequalities against the scan before model-visible use.

accepted_units.title: Positive-proportion separation and displacement are tied to two mean-value problems
accepted_units.why_material: States noncoincidence for a positive proportion of zeros, two-sided large displacement on positive proportions, an almost-all displacement bound, and identifies shifted versus unshifted argument-function differences as the respective analytic inputs.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose conclusions and the shifted/unshifted distinction are legible; several displayed bounds and subscripts are not reliable OCR.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires scan verification for constants, exponents, quantifiers embedded in formulas, and the exact normalization of S(t,chi).

accepted_units.title: Prime-coefficient variance drives the shifted argument-difference moment
accepted_units.why_material: The proof chooses coefficients from the character difference with a shift-dependent phase, invokes prior approximation estimates, uses Mertens's theorem to identify the prime-sum scale, and feeds that scale into the moment formula for Lemma 1.
accepted_units.context_note: The logical sequence is explicit in the prose at lines 171, 178-181, 197-200, and 200-206, while intervening displays are degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; the coefficient definition, prime sums, main constant, and error term must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Removing the shift changes the prime-sum scale used for Lemma 2
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the second moment input with the shifted case: the coefficient is the direct character difference, a Mertens estimate gives a log-log scale, and the conclusion follows by the preceding moment argument.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison and stated 2 log log scale are prose-recoverable despite a largely unreadable displayed sum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Scan verification is required for the sum, cutoff choice, error term, and exact parameter restrictions.

accepted_units.title: Argument increments become relative zero-count excursions
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the zero-counting formula to identify increments of the difference N(t,chi1)-N(t,chi2) with shifted increments of S(t,chi1)-S(t,chi2), yielding positive-measure positive and negative excursions under Lemma 1.
accepted_units.context_note: The zero-counting identity, the word 'essentially,' and the positive-proportion corollary are readable; the exact displayed powers are damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the normalization and endpoint convention for N and S; all numerical exponents and constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Moment information is converted into a positive-measure excursion set
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the zero-count difference f, introduces a threshold set and its characteristic function, combines moment bounds with Hölder's inequality, and chooses parameters so the set above the threshold has positive measure; the negative case is obtained by the analogous signed argument.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof architecture is explicit in the prose and named inequalities, but the displayed exponents and constants are unreliable OCR.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires scan verification of every moment exponent, threshold condition, parameter choice, and measure lower bound before quantitative reuse.

accepted_units.title: A zero-count excursion forces an empty interval between consecutive zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Turns the positive-proportion zero-count conclusion into the geometric assertion that, for the corresponding index, an interval between consecutive zeros of one L-function contains no zero of the other, completing the route to Theorem 1.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose implication and conclusion are readable although the first displayed inequality is badly extracted.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the ordered-zero convention and the exact sign/size of the preceding zero-count inequality; verify the display against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Index displacement is rewritten through zero counts and argument differences
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from the definition of A_n, expresses it via a zero count evaluated at a zero ordinate, substitutes the zero-counting relation, and derives even- and odd-moment estimates for the displacement sequence.
accepted_units.context_note: The sequence of transformations and the existence of the moment conclusions are visible, but most formulas in this span are substantially corrupted.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly scan-dependent: the exact identity, averaging range, normalization, factorial constant, error terms, and odd-moment statement must all be verified.

accepted_units.title: Displacement moments yield an almost-all growing-window bound
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a normalized empirical distribution of the displacement, invokes the moments obtained in the preceding subsection and a moment-determined distribution, then concludes that displacement exceeds a shrinking normalized threshold for almost all indices when the auxiliary function tends to infinity.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose route from moments to a distribution function and then to the almost-all statement is legible; the distribution display and normalization are OCR-damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires scan verification of the empirical distribution definition, limiting density, normalization by square-root log-log growth, and inequality direction.

accepted_units.title: The positive-proportion separation argument extends to unequal moduli
accepted_units.why_material: Records that the common-modulus assumption is not needed for Theorem 1 because the zero-count corollary acquires an explicit modulus-dependent adjustment rather than breaking the method.
accepted_units.context_note: The qualitative relaxation is clear in prose; the adjusted inequality is poorly extracted.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The correction term, signs, and dependence on the two moduli must be verified against the scan.
